newsitem.title: USA: Clinton urges AMR, pilots to reach agreement.
newsitem.headline: Clinton urges AMR, pilots to reach agreement.

text.p: President Bill Clinton Wednesday urged AMR Corp.'s American Airlines and its pilots to use the current federal mediation process to avert a possible strike.

"I have been following it very closely," Clinton told reporters at an unrelated White House event. "Today I want to say that the time has not expired, and I want to encourage parties to make maximum use of the mediation board process. That's what ought to be done today."
"This issue has huge implications for our country, and in particular for specific parts of our country," Clinton said. He was responding to a question asked at a White House event on aviation safety.

American, the nation's second largest carrier, and the Allied Pilots Association are negotiating under the auspices of a federal mediator. A strike by 9,000 pilots would occur at midnight Friday unless a new contract can be reached.

Officials from both sides reached a tentative accord last September, but the pilots' rank-and-file rejected it in December, leading to the strike deadline and the federally mediated bagaining. The dispute involves pay and other issues.

Clinton could intervene and declare a national emergency under the Railway Labour Act, which also applies to airlines, in order to keep American Airlines' planes flying. In November 1993 Clinton helped end a strike by American Airline flight attendants when he appealed to both sides to submit to arbitration.
